brief: A Goldman "Thoughts from the Floor" note synthesizing GCEM Macro Symposium soundbites and four trade recommendations. Fed speakers say the FOMC hiked as the committee views policy as still accommodative after years of missed inflation targets, with roughly 100bp of cumulative hikes now priced; strategists argue the committee's credibility keeps the long end relatively insulated even as AI-driven issuance and fiscal deficits add term-premium pressure. The core market vulnerability GS flags is oil: Hormuz has proven easier for Iran to close than the US can reopen, China's demand offset is fading, and every 10% sustained cut to Mideast exports is estimated to add ~$20/bbl to fair value, even though current supply/demand data still caps prices below the $125+ right-tail. A parallel scenario has European gas prices forcing ECB/CEE hikes if TTF and oil spike. Because clients are broadly long EM carry, frontier FX, equities/tech and received EM local rates, GS recommends four hedges against an oil-driven yields-up/equities-down shock: SPX lookback puts contingent on higher SOFR, USD binary calls vs CHF/EUR, QQQ dual/tri-binaries linked to yields and Brent, and outright Brent calls.
